title: Eureka: Human-Level Reward Design via Coding Large Language Models

mechanism.domainTask: LLM-based reward-function design for reinforcement-learning tasks
mechanism.populationDetail: Each iteration has a temporary batch of K sampled rewards, but only one global best reward is carried forward as the search state.
mechanism.archiveDetail: A single best-so-far reward is retained and updated only when an iteration's best score exceeds it.
mechanism.replacementDetail: Temporary candidate batches are evaluated per iteration; the paper does not describe a persistent population pool.
mechanism.generationDetail: The first batch is sampled independently from task/environment context; subsequent offspring broadly modify one best reward using its reflection.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Component values and policy metrics are structured feedback; the reward reflection is a textual interpretation of them.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: The best reward of the previous iteration is the parent after initialization; the initial batch has no parent.

provenance.citationWarning: Population/archive labels map a single best-so-far incumbent onto the survey taxonomy; repeated evaluation is final-only, not per-candidate.
